operations.title: Classical Sub-subleading Soft Photon and Soft Graviton Theorems in Four Spacetime Dimensions
The universal leading logarithmic tail does not canonically fix the finite tail scale

operations.reason: The source obtains the leading nonanalytic term from the ordered region omega << |ell| << L^{-1}, producing log(omega L), while explicitly discarding lower logarithmic orders and describing L only as larger than the object/scattering scale. Rescaling L preserves the leading log-squared coefficient and shifts precisely the subleading log and finite tail data. Thus the universal coefficient is source-defined, but the finite renormalized control is not fixed at this approximation order.

evidence.paraphrase: The primary TeX source defines the ordered integration window using L, obtains one-half omega log-squared(omega L), and systematically neglects lower logarithmic orders.
